nodes.summary: For elements $h$ and $g$ of a group and a natural number $l$, the iterated commutator $[h, g; l]$ is defined by $[h, g; 0] = h$ and $[h, g; l + 1] = [[h, g; l], g]$, where $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$; in particular $[h, g; 1] = [h, g]$.
nodes.title: Iterated commutators for Engel lengths

nodes.summary: There is a group $G$ such that for every polynomial $\varphi(x, y)$ in two variables with natural-number coefficients there are $u, v \in G$ such that $u$, $v$ and $uv$ are Engel elements and $l(uv) > \varphi(l(u), l(v))$. Here $g \in G$ is an Engel element if there is a $k \ge 1$ with $[h, g; k] = 1$ for all $h \in G$, and its Engel length $l(g)$ is the least such $k$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$,…
nodes.title: Engel lengths of products admit no polynomial bound (Kourovka 11.88)

nodes.summary: The statement that every group $G$ has a polynomial $\varphi(x, y)$ in two variables with natural-number coefficients such that $l(uv) \le \varphi(l(u), l(v))$ for all $u, v \in G$ for which $u$, $v$ and $uv$ are Engel elements. Here $g \in G$ is an Engel element if there is a $k \ge 1$ with $[h, g; k] = 1$ for all $h \in G$, and its Engel length $l(g)$ is the least such $k$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$,…
nodes.title: Roman'kov's problem on Engel lengths of products (Kourovka 11.88)

nodes.summary: For an element $g$ of a group $G$, the Engel length $l(g)$ is the least $k \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; k] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$. If no such $k$ exists, that is, if $g$ is not an Engel element, then $l(g) = 0$.
nodes.title: Engel length

nodes.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ there is an $n \ge 0$ with $h_n = 1$, where $h_0 = h$ and $h_{i + 1} = [h_i, g]$ with $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$; that is, some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Engel element

nodes.summary: An element $g$ of a group $G$ is an Engel element if there is an $l \ge 1$ such that $[h, g; l] = 1$ for every $h \in G$, where $[h, g; 0] = h$, $[h, g; i + 1] = [[h, g; i], g]$ and $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$.
nodes.title: Bounded Engel element

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, an element $a$ of a group $G$ is a right $n$-Engel element when $[a, {}_n x] = 1$ for every $x \in G$, where $[y, x] = y^{-1} x^{-1} y x$ and $[a, {}_n x] = [\dots[[a, x], x], \dots, x]$ is the left-normed commutator with $n$ copies of $x$ (so $[a, {}_0 x] = a$).
nodes.title: Right Engel element

nodes.summary: For elements $x$ and $y$ of a group, the commutator is $[x, y] = x^{-1} y^{-1} x y$ (the convention of the Kourovka Notebook).
nodes.title: Commutator for Engel lengths

nodes.summary: There are functions $e, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(n) > 0$ for every $n$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every nilpotent group $G$ and every normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ all of whose elements are right $n$-Engel elements of $G$, the subgroup $H^{e(n)}$ generated by the $e(n)$-th powers of elements of $H$ is contained in the $c(n)$-th term $\zeta_{c(n)}(G)$ of the upper central series of $G$.
nodes.title: Positive answer to Abdollahi's question on right Engel subgroups (Kourovka Problem 17.12)

nodes.summary: The statement that there are functions $e, c \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(n) > 0$ for every $n$ such that, for every natural number $n$, every nilpotent group $G$ and every normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ all of whose elements are right $n$-Engel elements of $G$, the subgroup $H^{e(n)}$ generated by the $e(n)$-th powers of elements of $H$ is contained in the $c(n)$-th term $\zeta_{c(n)}(G)$ of the upper…
nodes.title: Abdollahi's question on right Engel subgroups (Kourovka Problem 17.12)

nodes.summary: There is a non-abelian simple group $G$ (one with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$) that contains an Engel element $g \ne 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.
nodes.title: Non-abelian simple groups can have nontrivial Engel elements (Kourovka 16.17)

nodes.summary: The statement that no non-abelian simple group contains an Engel element other than the identity: for every simple group $G$ with elements $a$, $b$ such that $ab \ne ba$, every Engel element $g$ of $G$ satisfies $g = 1$. Here $g$ is an Engel element if for every $h \in G$ some iterated commutator $[h, g, \dots, g]$ is trivial, where $[x, g] = x^{-1} g^{-1} x g$.
nodes.title: Bludov's problem on Engel elements in simple groups (Kourovka 16.17)
